beats.text: Two parents, one child, one deposit. Every month the Canada Child Benefit lands in Maya's account, never Dan's. It's not a mistake.
Maya and Dan live together with their four-year-old. Right now that's up to eight thousand one hundred and fifty-seven dollars a year.
But the CRA pays only one person per home. And the law presumes the mother is primarily responsible for the child, so she applies.
If Dan does most of the caregiving, he can apply instead, with a signed letter from Maya saying so.
Same-sex parents? One of you applies for all the children, and you choose who.
The twist: switching who gets it doesn't change the amount by a cent. The CRA says it's the same, no matter which parent receives it.
So pick who applies, and keep filing your returns every year.
Next: separated parents and shared custody, who gets the benefit then? Follow so you don't miss it.
